question.problem:
Determine if the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}10 & -4 \\ 24 & -10\end{aligned}]$ 
is diagonalizable or not, and if it is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}10-\lambda  & -4 \\ 24 & -10-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (10-\lambda )(-10-\lambda )-24\cdot (-4) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Since we get two distinct eigenvalues, the matrix $A$ is diagonalizable.

Now, we construct the diagonal matrix $D,$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$
